observations: Large office photocopier/printer wrapped in clear plastic film.
The brand 'SHARP' and model 'AR-M207' are clearly printed on the front panel in photos 0, 1, and 2.
A 'digital' logo is visible on the right side in photo 1.
Two paper trays are visible at the bottom, labeled 'A4' and 'A3' in photo 1.
The machine is shown in a storage or warehouse environment, sitting on wooden pallets.
All photos contain a watermark for 'SMATECH MEGA EQUIPMENT'.

claims.evidence: Requires a photo of the status page or the digital counter on the display.

claims.claim: New drum and toner just fitted
claims.evidence: Requires a printed supply status report.
Requires a video of the machine successfully completing a multi-page copy or print job.

risks.risk: The machine may not power on or may have internal electronic faults.
risks.proof: A video of the machine powering up to a 'Ready' state.

risks.risk: The print quality could be poor (streaks, spots, or fading) despite claims of new consumables.
risks.proof: A photo of a high-quality test print or configuration page produced by the machine.
risks.if_unproven: as needing a new drum and toner

risks.risk: The plastic wrap may be hiding significant cosmetic damage, cracks, or missing panels.
risks.proof: Photos of the machine from all angles with the plastic wrap removed.

risks.risk: The actual page count could be much higher than 20,000.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the total counter on the LCD screen or a printed report.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powered on and performing a successful copy operation.
Photo of the LCD screen showing the total copy/print count.
Photo of a printed status or configuration page to verify print quality and toner levels.
Photos of the machine with the plastic wrap removed to inspect the exterior condition.
response.reason: The model is clearly identified. Because it is wrapped and not shown operational, it is priced at the worst-case value of a non-functional unit for parts or refurbishment.
